batch_1.title: Marry Me Chicken
batch_1.description: Golden pan-seared chicken cutlets in a creamy sun-dried tomato and Parmesan sauce, ready in 40 minutes.
secondary_keywords: marry me chicken without heavy cream
can you freeze marry me chicken
intro: Marry Me Chicken is thin chicken cutlets seared until golden, then finished in a cream sauce built on sun-dried tomatoes, garlic, chicken broth and Parmesan. The name is a joke about how good it is; the method is a plain skillet dinner that takes about 40 minutes and one pan.

It works because each ingredient has a job. Slicing the breasts into cutlets means they cook through in the time it takes to brown them. A light coat of flour gives the sauce something to cling to. Sun-dried tomatoes bring concentrated sweetness and acid that keep the cream from tasting flat.

The result is rich but not heavy: a glossy, pale-orange sauce with a savory-sweet edge, tender chicken and a little heat from red pepper flakes. Serve it over pasta, rice or mashed potatoes to catch the sauce.

key_ingredients.name: Chicken breasts
key_ingredients.role: Sliced into thin cutlets so they cook evenly in about 8 minutes total and stay juicy.

key_ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes
key_ingredients.role: Oil-packed tomatoes add sweetness, acidity and color, and the oil flavors the sauce.

key_ingredients.name: Heavy cream
key_ingredients.role: Provides body, and its high fat content keeps the sauce from splitting at a simmer.

key_ingredients.name: Parmesan
key_ingredients.role: Adds salt and savory depth; grate it fresh so it melts smooth.

key_ingredients.name: All-purpose flour
key_ingredients.role: A light dredge browns the chicken and thickens the sauce slightly.

ingredients: 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 1 1/2 lb / 680 g total)
1/3 cup (about 40 g) oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drained and chopped
1/2 cup (50 g) freshly grated Parmesan cheese
2 tbsp chopped fresh basil or parsley
instructions: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 8 thin cutlets. Pat them dry with paper towels, then season both sides with 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and the black pepper.
Spread the flour on a plate and dredge each cutlet, shaking off the excess so only a thin coat remains.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Cook the cutlets in two batches, about 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and an instant-read thermometer reads 165°F (74°C). Transfer to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and melt the butter in the same pan. Add the garlic, sun-dried tomatoes and red pepper flakes and cook for 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant.
Pour in the broth and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in the cream, Italian seasoning and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt. Simmer gently for 4 to 5 minutes, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the Parmesan until melted and smooth. Return the chicken and any juices from the plate to the pan and spoon the sauce over the top.
Let the chicken warm through for 2 minutes, then scatter with basil and serve right away.
pro_tips: Slice the chicken while it is very cold, or after 15 minutes in the freezer, and use a sharp knife with the flat of your hand on top. Cutlets of even thickness, about 1/2 inch, are what make the timing work.
Do not crowd the pan. If the cutlets touch, they steam instead of browning, and the browned bits left behind are the base of the sauce's flavor.
Add the Parmesan off the heat. Cheese stirred into a boiling sauce turns grainy, and pre-shredded cheese, which carries anti-caking starch, melts less smoothly than a block you grate yourself.
The sauce thickens as it stands. If it tightens before you serve, stir in a splash of broth or cream over low heat until it flows again.
substitutions: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs work in place of breasts; pound them to an even thickness and cook to 175°F (79°C) for the best texture.
Use half-and-half instead of heavy cream for a lighter sauce and simmer a minute longer; it is less forgiving and can separate if it boils hard.
Stir a couple of handfuls of fresh baby spinach into the sauce with the cream to add greens without changing the flavor.

variations.air_fryer: Air fry the dredged cutlets at 400°F (200°C) for 8 to 10 minutes, flipping once and spraying lightly with oil, until they reach 165°F. Make the sauce in a skillet while they cook, then toss the chicken in to warm through for a minute. The crust will be paler than with pan-searing.
variations.slow_cooker: Set plain chicken breasts in a 6-quart slow cooker with the garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, broth and Italian seasoning. Cook on low for 3 to 4 hours, until the chicken reaches 165°F, then stir in the cream and Parmesan for the last 15 minutes. The chicken will be tender rather than seared, and the sauce looser.

diet.low_carb: Skip the flour and pat the chicken very dry before searing. Per serving the dish drops to about 5 grams of carbohydrate, most of it from the cream and tomatoes.
diet.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free all-purpose flour blend or 2 tablespoons of cornstarch for the dredge, and check that the broth and Italian seasoning are labeled gluten-free.
diet.vegan: The dish is built on chicken and dairy, so there is no direct swap. For a plant-based version, sear thick slices of cauliflower or firm tofu and use full-fat coconut cream and nutritional yeast in the sauce; the flavor is different but the method carries over.

batch_1.storage_tips: Cool leftovers within 2 hours and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days. This dish does not freeze well because the cream sauce can separate on thawing; if you plan ahead, freeze only the cooked chicken for up to 2 months and make the sauce fresh. Reheat gently in a skillet over low heat with a splash of broth or cream, stirring, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) again. In the microwave, use 50 percent power and stir halfway to avoid a broken sauce.

faqs.question: Why is it called Marry Me Chicken?
faqs.answer: The name is a joke: the dish is said to be so good that it inspires proposals. There is nothing special in the recipe beyond a well-made cream sauce; the name comes from social media rather than from a traditional dish.

faqs.question: Can I make Marry Me Chicken without heavy cream?
faqs.answer: Yes, though the texture changes. Half-and-half gives a lighter sauce that needs an extra minute of simmering and gentler heat, and evaporated milk works in a pinch. Full-fat coconut milk is a dairy-free option with a mild coconut flavor.

faqs.question: What should I serve with Marry Me Chicken?
faqs.answer: Anything that catches sauce: linguine, penne, rice, mashed potatoes or crusty bread. A green vegetable such as roasted broccoli, green beans or a simple arugula salad balances the richness.

faqs.question: How do I know when the chicken is done?
faqs.answer: Use an instant-read thermometer: chicken is safe at 165°F (74°C) in the thickest part. Thin cutlets usually reach it in 4 minutes per side, and they finish warming in the sauce, so it is better to pull them just at temperature than to overcook them in the pan.

batch_1.title: White Chicken Chili
batch_1.description: Creamy tomato-free chili with tender shredded chicken, white beans and green chiles, finished with cream cheese for a thick, mild-spiced bowl.
secondary_keywords: white chicken chili with great northern beans
can you freeze white chicken chili
intro: White chicken chili is a pale, tomato-free cousin of the classic red bowl: shredded chicken and white beans in a broth flavored with green chiles, cumin and oregano, thickened with cream cheese. It is milder than red chili, with a gentle heat that builds from the chiles rather than from chili powder.

Two steps make it thick without flour. Mashing about a cup of the beans releases their starch into the broth, and the cream cheese melts in at the end for body and a slight tang. Poaching the chicken breasts whole in the simmering pot keeps them tender and seasons the broth at the same time.

The finished chili is creamy but not heavy, with bright lime at the end to cut through the beans and cheese. It comes together in about 50 minutes, holds well on the stove for a crowd, and is better with a topping bar of cheese, cilantro, tortilla chips and avocado.

key_ingredients.name: Great Northern beans
key_ingredients.role: Mild, creamy white beans that hold their shape; canned works and saves hours.

key_ingredients.name: Green chiles
key_ingredients.role: Canned diced mild green chiles provide roasted, slightly smoky flavor with little heat.

key_ingredients.name: Chicken breasts
key_ingredients.role: Poached whole in the broth, then shredded so the meat stays juicy.

key_ingredients.name: Cream cheese
key_ingredients.role: Melts into the broth for body and a mild tang without flour.

key_ingredients.name: Lime juice
key_ingredients.role: A squeeze at the end lifts the whole pot.

ingredients: 2 (4 oz / 113 g) cans diced mild green chiles
2 (15 oz / 425 g) cans Great Northern beans, drained and rinsed
1 1/2 lb (680 g) boneless, skinless chicken breasts
4 oz (113 g) cream cheese, cut into cubes
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 cup (4 oz / 113 g) shredded Monterey Jack cheese, for serving
1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro, for serving
instructions: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, oregano and coriander and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the green chiles.

Add the beans, broth, salt and pepper, then nestle in the whole chicken breasts. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat to a steady simmer, cover and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and shred it with two forks.
Scoop about 1 cup of the beans and a little broth into a bowl, mash them into a rough paste and stir it back into the pot to thicken the chili.
Add the cream cheese, half-and-half and corn. Stir over low heat for 4 to 5 minutes, until the cream cheese has melted completely and the chili is hot.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the lime juice and taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with the Monterey Jack and cilantro.
pro_tips: Cook the spices in the hot oil for 30 seconds before adding liquid. Ground spices are fat-soluble, and this brief toasting deepens their flavor far more than stirring them into the broth.
Keep the simmer gentle while the chicken cooks. A hard boil toughens breast meat; small, lazy bubbles cook it evenly and leave it easy to shred.
Add the cream cheese and half-and-half over low heat and do not boil afterward. Dairy stirred into a hard-boiling, acidic pot can look curdled.
Season at the end. Canned beans, chiles and broth all carry salt, so taste after the dairy and lime go in before adding more.
substitutions: Chicken thighs work in place of breasts and stay juicier; simmer them 20 to 25 minutes, until they reach 175°F (79°C).
Swap the cream cheese and half-and-half for 1/2 cup of sour cream stirred in off the heat, or use plain Greek yogurt for a tangier finish.
Cannellini or navy beans replace Great Northern beans one for one.

variations.air_fryer: The air fryer is not suited to a brothy chili, but it can cook the chicken. Rub the breasts with oil, salt and cumin, air fry at 375°F (190°C) for 15 to 18 minutes until they reach 165°F, then shred and stir into a chili base made on the stove.
variations.slow_cooker: Add everything except the cream cheese, half-and-half, corn and lime to a 6-quart slow cooker. Cook on low for 6 to 7 hours or on high for 3 to 4, shred the chicken, then stir in the dairy, corn and lime and cook 20 minutes more. In an Instant Pot, pressure cook on high for 10 minutes with a 10-minute natural release, shred, then finish with the dairy on the sauté setting.

diet.low_carb: Beans supply most of the carbohydrate here, roughly 100 grams across the whole pot, so a true low-carb version is not practical. Replacing half the beans with diced cauliflower or zucchini reduces the load but changes the texture.
diet.gluten_free: The recipe is gluten-free as written; check the labels on the broth, chiles and cream cheese, since some brands add wheat-based thickeners.
diet.vegan: Use vegetable broth, replace the chicken with an extra can of beans and 2 cups of diced roasted sweet potato or cauliflower, and stir in 1/2 cup of cashew cream or full-fat coconut milk in place of the dairy.

batch_1.storage_tips: Cool the chili within 2 hours and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Freeze it for up to 3 months; for the best texture, freeze before adding the cream cheese and half-and-half and stir them in when you reheat. Thaw overnight in the fridge. Reheat on the stove over medium-low heat, stirring often, for 10 to 12 minutes until it is steaming hot and reaches 165°F (74°C), adding a splash of broth if it has thickened.

faqs.question: How do I thicken white chicken chili?
faqs.answer: Mash about a cup of the beans and stir them back in; the released starch thickens the broth. Simmering uncovered for 5 to 10 minutes also reduces it, and the cream cheese adds body at the end.

faqs.question: Can I use canned or rotisserie chicken?
faqs.answer: Yes. Stir 3 to 4 cups of shredded rotisserie chicken in at the end and skip the poaching step; add it after the dairy so it only needs to warm through, about 5 minutes.

faqs.question: Is white chicken chili spicy?
faqs.answer: It is mild. Mild canned green chiles add flavor rather than heat. For more heat, add a diced jalapeño with the onion, 1/4 teaspoon of cayenne with the spices or a splash of hot sauce at the table.

faqs.question: What are the best toppings for white chicken chili?
faqs.answer: Shredded Monterey Jack or pepper jack, chopped cilantro, sliced avocado, crushed tortilla chips, a spoonful of sour cream and lime wedges are the classic set; pickled jalapeños add heat and acid.

batch_1.title: Lasagna Soup
batch_1.description: All the flavors of baked lasagna in one pot: Italian sausage, tomatoes and broken noodles topped with ricotta, Parmesan and melted mozzarella.
intro: Lasagna soup takes the flavors of a baked lasagna, including sausage, tomatoes, garlic, oregano and cheese, and turns them into an easy pot dinner you can finish in about 50 minutes. There is no layering, no oven and no waiting for a pan to set.

Broken lasagna noodles cook directly in the tomato broth, so they release a little starch that gives the soup body, and there is no separate pot to boil. The ricotta topping is the part that makes it taste like lasagna rather than pasta soup: a spoonful of ricotta, Parmesan and basil melts slowly into the hot broth.
The texture is hearty and spoonable, with tender ribbons of pasta, browned sausage and a bright tomato base. It is filling enough to serve as a full meal with crusty bread.

key_ingredients.name: Italian sausage
key_ingredients.role: Supplies fat, fennel and seasoning, so the broth tastes developed without a long simmer.

key_ingredients.name: Crushed tomatoes and tomato paste
key_ingredients.role: Crushed tomatoes give body; a spoonful of paste, cooked for a minute, adds depth.

key_ingredients.name: Lasagna noodles
key_ingredients.role: Broken into 1- to 2-inch pieces, they cook in the soup and thicken it slightly.

key_ingredients.name: Ricotta and Parmesan topping
key_ingredients.role: Creamy and salty, it stands in for the cheese layer of a baked lasagna.

key_ingredients.name: Mozzarella
key_ingredients.role: Melts into stretchy strands on top of each bowl.

ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) Italian sausage, mild or hot, casings removed
4 cups (960 ml) low-sodium chicken or beef broth
1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, optional
1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
6 dry lasagna noodles (about 6 oz / 170 g), broken into 1- to 2-inch pieces
1/2 cup (50 g) freshly grated Parmesan cheese, divided
1 cup (4 oz / 113 g) shredded low-moisture mozzarella cheese
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or soup pot over medium-high heat. Add the sausage and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles, until browned and cooked through. Spoon off all but about 1 tablespoon of the fat.
Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until softened. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute until the paste darkens slightly.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and broth. Add the oregano, dried basil, pepper flakes, salt and black pepper, and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer, partly covered, for 10 minutes so the flavors combine.
Stir in the broken lasagna noodles. Simmer uncovered for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often so they do not stick, until the noodles are just tender.
While the noodles cook, stir the ricotta with half of the Parmesan and a pinch of salt in a small bowl.
Taste the soup and adjust the salt. Stir in half of the mozzarella and let it melt for 1 minute.
Ladle into bowls and top each with a spoonful of the ricotta mixture, the remaining mozzarella and Parmesan, and fresh basil.
pro_tips: Break the noodles small and stir them often for the first 3 minutes. Broken lasagna sheets are wide and sticky, and they clump if left alone in the pot.
Pull the soup off the heat when the noodles are just tender. They keep absorbing broth, and a soup that looks perfect on the stove will be thick and stodgy by the time you serve it.
Drain most of the sausage fat before cooking the onion. Some fat is flavor, but too much leaves the tomato broth greasy on top.
Use whole-milk ricotta. Part-skim ricotta is drier and can turn grainy when it meets hot broth.
substitutions: Ground beef, ground turkey or chicken sausage replace the Italian sausage; add 1/2 teaspoon of fennel seeds and an extra pinch of salt if you use plain ground meat.
Broken mafalde, fusilli or another short pasta can replace the lasagna noodles; use about 6 ounces and check the package for cook time.
Drained cottage cheese, stirred with the Parmesan, replaces ricotta in the topping.

variations.air_fryer: The air fryer is not suited to a brothy soup, but it can make a crisp topping. Toss torn bread or a handful of panko with oil and Parmesan and air fry at 375°F (190°C) for 3 to 4 minutes for crunchy croutons to scatter over each bowl.
variations.slow_cooker: Brown the sausage, onion and garlic first, then add them to a 6-quart slow cooker with the tomatoes, broth and seasonings. Cook on low for 6 hours or high for 3. Add the broken noodles for the last 20 to 30 minutes on high, checking often, because they turn soft quickly, and add the cheeses when serving. In an Instant Pot, use the sauté setting for the browning and cook the noodles in the simmering soup as written; pressure cooking pasta in a chunky soup can leave it overcooked.

diet.low_carb: The noodles supply about 125 grams of carbohydrate for the whole pot. Leaving them out and adding diced zucchini for the last 5 minutes lowers the carbohydrate per bowl by more than half.
diet.gluten_free: Use gluten-free lasagna noodles or brown-rice pasta, and check the sausage and broth labels for wheat. Gluten-free pasta softens faster, so add it for the last 6 to 8 minutes and expect the soup to thicken less.
diet.vegan: Replace the sausage with 8 ounces of chopped mushrooms and a can of drained lentils, use vegetable broth, and top with cashew ricotta or a dairy-free mozzarella. The flavor is lighter but the method is unchanged.

batch_1.storage_tips: Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 4 days. The noodles keep absorbing liquid, so expect the soup to thicken; stir in 1/2 cup of broth or water per serving when reheating. You can freeze the soup for up to 2 months, though the noodles soften; for the best result, freeze the soup without noodles and cook fresh noodles when you reheat. Reheat on the stove over medium heat until steaming hot, or microwave in 60-second bursts, stirring between each. Add the ricotta topping fresh.

faqs.question: Can I make lasagna soup without sausage?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ground beef, ground turkey or chopped mushrooms all work. Meat other than sausage has less seasoning, so add 1/2 teaspoon of fennel seed and an extra pinch of salt and pepper flakes.

faqs.question: Why did my lasagna soup turn thick?
faqs.answer: The noodles continue to absorb broth as the soup sits. Stir in warm broth or water a splash at a time until it loosens, and next time pull the pot off the heat when the noodles are just tender.

faqs.question: Can I use no-boil lasagna noodles?
faqs.answer: Yes. Break them into pieces and add them for the last 6 to 8 minutes; they soften faster than regular noodles and can turn mushy if simmered for 10 minutes or more.

faqs.question: Can you freeze lasagna soup?
faqs.answer: Yes, for up to 2 months. Freeze it without the noodles or ricotta topping for the best texture, then add freshly cooked noodles and the topping when you reheat.

batch_1.title: Air Fryer Chicken Breast
batch_1.description: Juicy air fryer chicken breasts with a smoky paprika rub, cooked in about 18 minutes with no breading and no mess.
secondary_keywords: how long to cook chicken breast in air fryer
can you freeze air fryer chicken breast
intro: This air fryer chicken breast is seasoned with paprika, garlic and onion powder and cooks in 15 to 18 minutes with a light coat of oil. There is no breading, no preheating a full-size oven and no pan to scrub.

An air fryer is a small convection oven: a fan pushes hot air around the food, which browns the surface quickly while the inside stays moist. That speed is exactly what lean chicken breast needs, provided the pieces are the same thickness. Pounding the thick end down to about 3/4 inch is the one step that decides whether every breast finishes at the same time.

The result is chicken with a lightly browned, savory exterior and tender, juicy slices, ready for meal prep, salads, sandwiches or a quick dinner with vegetables. It also reheats well, which is why one batch can cover dinner tonight and lunches later in the week.

key_ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts
key_ingredients.role: Six- to eight-ounce breasts, pounded to an even 3/4 inch, cook uniformly.

key_ingredients.name: Olive oil
key_ingredients.role: A tablespoon helps the rub cling and promotes browning in the dry heat.

key_ingredients.name: Smoked paprika
key_ingredients.role: Adds color and a grill-like savoriness without extra time.

key_ingredients.name: Garlic and onion powder
key_ingredients.role: Powders stay on the surface without burning the way fresh garlic would in high heat.

key_ingredients.name: Kosher salt
key_ingredients.role: Seasons the meat; salting 10 minutes ahead helps the chicken stay juicy.

ingredients: 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts (6 to 8 oz / 170 to 225 g each)
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap or parchment and pound the thickest part with a meat mallet or rolling pin until the breast is an even 3/4 inch thick.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels. Rub with the olive oil, then season both sides with the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper. Let stand for 10 minutes.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F (190°C) for 3 minutes.
Arrange the chicken in a single layer in the basket with space between the pieces. Cook in two batches if your basket is small.
Air fry for 8 minutes, flip the breasts, then cook another 6 to 9 minutes until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part reads 165°F (74°C).
Transfer to a cutting board and rest for 5 minutes so the juices redistribute.
Slice against the grain and serve with lemon wedges.
pro_tips: Pound the breasts to an even thickness. A breast that is thick at one end and thin at the other overcooks in the thin half before the thick half is done, which is the main reason air fryer chicken turns dry.
Trust a thermometer, not the clock. Air fryers vary by model and basket size, so pull the chicken at 165°F (74°C); it will rise a degree or two while it rests.
Do not crowd the basket. The hot air has to circulate around each piece, and overlapping breasts steam and brown unevenly.
Pat the surface dry before oiling. Moisture on the chicken slows browning, and the oil and spices slide off a wet surface.
substitutions: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs work in place of breasts; cook at 375°F (190°C) for 10 to 14 minutes to an internal temperature of 175°F (79°C) for the best texture.
Use taco seasoning, Cajun seasoning or lemon pepper instead of the paprika blend, but check the sodium first because blends are often salty.
Avocado oil replaces olive oil; it has a higher smoke point and suits the hot air of the fryer.

variations.air_fryer: This recipe is the air fryer method. For a crisp coating, dip the seasoned breasts in beaten egg, press them into panko mixed with Parmesan, spray with oil and cook at 375°F for 12 to 16 minutes, flipping once, until golden and 165°F inside.
variations.slow_cooker: A slow cooker does the opposite of what this recipe is about. Chicken breasts cooked on low for 3 to 4 hours (or on high for 2 to 3) with 1/2 cup of broth turn out very tender and shreddable rather than browned, which suits tacos, sandwiches and salads. Check at the low end, because breast meat dries out quickly.

diet.low_carb: Chicken breast with a dry rub is naturally low in carbohydrate, at about 1 gram per serving. Keep the coating off and serve with roasted vegetables or a green salad.
diet.gluten_free: The recipe is gluten-free as written. Check that the spices and any seasoning blend you substitute are labeled gluten-free.
diet.vegan: Not applicable to chicken. For a plant-based version, use 1-inch slabs of extra-firm tofu, pressed and rubbed with the same spices, and air fry at 375°F for 12 to 15 minutes, flipping once.

batch_1.storage_tips: Let the chicken cool, then refrigerate it in an airtight container for up to 4 days. For meal prep, slice it after chilling. To freeze, wrap portions individually or store them in a freezer bag with the air pressed out for up to 3 months, and thaw overnight in the fridge. Reheat sliced chicken in the air fryer at 350°F (175°C) for 3 to 5 minutes, or in the microwave, covered, with a spoonful of water or broth in 30-second bursts, until it reaches 165°F (74°C).

faqs.question: How long do you cook chicken breast in the air fryer?
faqs.answer: At 375°F (190°C), breasts pounded to 3/4 inch take 14 to 17 minutes, flipping halfway. Thicker, unpounded breasts can take 18 to 22 minutes. The chicken is done at 165°F (74°C) in the thickest part.

faqs.question: Do I need to preheat the air fryer?
faqs.answer: A short 3-minute preheat helps the surface brown as soon as the chicken goes in. Many models do not require it, but the results are more consistent when the basket starts hot.

faqs.question: Why is my air fryer chicken dry?
faqs.answer: Usually the breasts are uneven or overcooked. Pound them to an even thickness, check the temperature early, remove the chicken at 165°F and rest it for 5 minutes before slicing.

faqs.question: Can I cook frozen chicken breasts in the air fryer?
faqs.answer: It is safer to thaw them in the refrigerator first. Frozen breasts cook unevenly, and the outside can dry out before the center is safe to eat; if you must cook from frozen, use a thermometer and expect a much longer cook time.

batch_1.title: Air Fryer Pork Chops
batch_1.description: Juicy bone-in pork chops with a smoky paprika and brown sugar rub, golden outside and tender inside in about 12 minutes.
secondary_keywords: how long to cook pork chops in air fryer
air fryer bone in pork chops
air fryer pork chops internal temperature
intro: These air fryer pork chops have a browned, savory crust and a juicy center after just 10 to 12 minutes at 400°F. The rub is a simple mix of smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, brown sugar, salt and pepper, and there is no marinade or breading to manage.

Pork loin chops are lean and unforgiving, which makes the air fryer a good fit: its fast, dry heat browns the outside before the inside has time to dry out. Choosing chops that are 1 inch thick and bone-in matters, because the bone slows heat on one side and thin chops cook through before they brown.

Pulled at 145°F and rested for 5 minutes, the pork stays juicy and slightly blush pink at the center, which is safe according to current USDA guidance. Serve it with applesauce, roasted potatoes or a simple green vegetable.

key_ingredients.name: Bone-in center-cut chops
key_ingredients.role: One-inch thickness and the bone keep the meat from drying out before it browns.

key_ingredients.name: Light brown sugar
key_ingredients.role: A small amount caramelizes in the hot air and helps the crust color.

key_ingredients.name: Smoked paprika
key_ingredients.role: Adds a smoky, grilled note and deep red color.

key_ingredients.name: Olive oil
key_ingredients.role: Helps the rub stick and the surface brown.

key_ingredients.name: Kosher salt
key_ingredients.role: Seasons the meat; salting 10 to 15 minutes ahead helps it retain moisture.

ingredients: 4 bone-in center-cut pork chops, 1 inch thick (about 8 oz / 225 g each)
instructions: Take the pork chops out of the refrigerator 20 minutes before cooking. Pat them completely dry with paper towels.
In a small bowl, mix the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, brown sugar, salt, pepper and thyme.
Rub the chops on both sides with the olive oil, then coat evenly with the spice mixture. Let stand for 10 minutes.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F (200°C) for 3 minutes.

Place the chops in a single layer in the basket without touching. Air fry for 5 to 6 minutes, flip, and cook another 5 to 6 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part, away from the bone, reads 145°F (63°C).
Transfer to a plate, tent loosely with foil and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Spoon any juices from the plate over the chops and serve.
pro_tips: Choose chops at least 1 inch thick. Thin chops overcook before they brown, and boneless thin chops often finish dry no matter what the recipe says.
Pull the pork at 145°F (63°C) and rest it for at least 3 minutes. It rises a few degrees while resting, and going past 150°F is when loin chops turn tough.
Pat the surface dry and do not overload the basket. Moisture and crowding are what produce pale, steamed chops instead of browned ones.
Wipe out sugar drips between batches. The brown sugar in the rub can burn on the basket and smoke at 400°F, so a quick clean keeps the second batch tasting clean.
substitutions: Boneless pork loin chops can be used, but cook them 1 to 2 minutes less per side and check the temperature early.
Use 1 teaspoon of maple syrup in place of the brown sugar, or leave the sugar out for a purely savory crust.
Swap the rub for Cajun seasoning, a store-bought pork rub or dried rosemary and lemon zest, keeping the salt in mind.

variations.air_fryer: This recipe is the air fryer method. For a breaded chop, dip the seasoned chops in beaten egg, press them into panko, spray with oil and cook at 400°F for 10 to 13 minutes, flipping once, until golden and 145°F inside.
variations.slow_cooker: Pork loin chops are a poor fit for a slow cooker, which dries lean meat over long cooking. If you want a slow cooker meal, use bone-in chops on low for 3 to 4 hours in lightly seasoned broth and expect tender but not seared meat, or use pork shoulder instead for pulled pork.

diet.low_carb: The chops are low in carbohydrate, at about 2 grams per serving. Omit the brown sugar to remove most of that, and serve with a green vegetable or salad.
diet.gluten_free: The recipe is gluten-free as written; check that any premixed spice rub you substitute has no wheat-based fillers.
diet.vegan: There is no direct swap for pork. For a plant-based dish with a similar rub and method, use thick slices of king oyster mushroom or extra-firm tofu and air fry at 375°F for 12 to 15 minutes, flipping once.

batch_1.storage_tips: Refrigerate cooked chops in an airtight container for up to 3 to 4 days. To freeze, wrap them individually and store in a freezer bag for up to 3 months, then thaw overnight in the fridge. Reheat in the air fryer at 350°F (175°C) for 4 to 5 minutes, or slice and warm in a covered skillet with a spoonful of broth so the meat does not dry out. Microwaving works in short 30-second bursts at 50 percent power, but the texture is less tender.

faqs.question: How long do you cook pork chops in the air fryer?
faqs.answer: One-inch bone-in chops take 10 to 12 minutes at 400°F (200°C), flipped halfway. Thinner chops take 8 to 10 minutes, and thicker ones 14 to 16. Always confirm with a thermometer rather than the clock.

faqs.question: What internal temperature should air fryer pork chops reach?
faqs.answer: The USDA recommends 145°F (63°C) followed by a 3-minute rest. A few degrees higher is fine for those who prefer no pink, but going much past 150°F risks dry meat.

faqs.question: Should I flip pork chops in the air fryer?
faqs.answer: Yes. Flipping halfway browns both sides evenly. If your air fryer has a strong top element you may find one side browns faster, so flip earlier and rotate the basket if needed.

faqs.question: Can I cook boneless pork chops the same way?
faqs.answer: Yes. Reduce the time by 1 to 2 minutes per side because boneless chops cook faster, and start checking the temperature at 8 minutes. Boneless chops dry out more easily, so a rest and a thermometer matter even more.

batch_1.title: Crockpot Potato Soup
batch_1.description: Creamy loaded potato soup made in the slow cooker with russets, cream cheese, bacon and cheddar; 20 minutes of prep, then it cooks itself.
intro: This Crockpot potato soup is a loaded baked potato in a bowl: tender russet potatoes cooked in broth with onion and garlic, partly mashed for body, then finished with cream cheese, half-and-half, crisp bacon and sharp cheddar. Twenty minutes of prep is all it needs before the slow cooker takes over, and any 6-quart slow cooker will do.

Russets are the right potato here. Their high starch breaks down as they cook and thickens the soup naturally, so no flour or roux is needed. Mashing about half the potatoes in the pot leaves plenty of tender chunks while making the base creamy.

The dairy goes in last so it stays smooth. The finished soup is thick, savory and mild, with salty bacon and cheddar on top and green onion for freshness. It serves eight, tastes better the next day, and needs nothing more than a green salad or crusty bread alongside.

key_ingredients.name: Russet potatoes
key_ingredients.role: High-starch potatoes that fall apart as they cook, thickening the soup without flour.

key_ingredients.name: Chicken broth
key_ingredients.role: Cooks the potatoes and supplies savory depth; low-sodium lets you control the salt.

key_ingredients.name: Cream cheese
key_ingredients.role: Melts into the base for richness and a slight tang.

key_ingredients.name: Half-and-half
key_ingredients.role: Loosens the soup and adds creaminess with less fat than heavy cream.

key_ingredients.name: Bacon and cheddar
key_ingredients.role: Provide salt, smoke and sharpness at the end, the flavors of a loaded baked potato.

ingredients: 3 lb (1.4 kg) russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
8 oz (225 g) cream cheese, cut into cubes and softened
6 slices bacon, cooked until crisp and crumbled
1 cup (4 oz / 113 g) shredded sharp cheddar cheese
1/2 cup (115 g) sour cream, for serving
instructions: Add the potatoes, onion, garlic, broth, salt, pepper and thyme to a 6-quart slow cooker and stir to combine.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours, or on high for 3 to 4 hours, until the potatoes are very tender and break apart easily when pressed with a fork.
Use a potato masher to crush about half of the potatoes right in the pot, leaving the rest in chunks. Stir in the cream cheese and half-and-half.
Cover and cook for 20 to 30 minutes more on high, stirring once or twice, until the cream cheese has melted and the soup is smooth and hot.
Stir in half of the bacon and half of the cheddar. Taste and add salt if needed.
Ladle into bowls and top with the remaining bacon, cheddar, green onions and a spoonful of sour cream.
pro_tips: Cut the potatoes into even 3/4-inch cubes. Big pieces take hours longer to soften, and uneven pieces leave a mix of mush and hard bits.
Add the dairy at the end. Cream cheese and half-and-half added at the beginning of a six-hour cook can curdle or turn grainy, and the flavor is duller.
Mash, do not blend. A potato masher keeps some texture, while a blender or immersion blender overworks the potato starch and turns the soup gluey.
Season with salt at the end. Bacon, cheddar and broth are all salty, so taste the finished soup before adding more.
substitutions: Yukon Gold potatoes work in place of russets and give a creamier, buttery flavor, but the soup will be slightly less thick, so mash a bit more of the potatoes.
Use whole milk instead of half-and-half for a lighter soup, or heavy cream for a richer one.
Cooked ham or crumbled smoked sausage, about 1 cup, can replace the bacon.

variations.air_fryer: The air fryer cannot cook a soup, but it makes crisp bacon quickly for the topping. Air fry the bacon slices at 375°F (190°C) for 6 to 9 minutes until crisp, then crumble them over the bowls.
variations.slow_cooker: This recipe is the slow cooker method. For an Instant Pot, sauté the onion and garlic, add the potatoes and broth, and pressure cook on high for 8 minutes with a quick release, then mash and stir in the dairy on the sauté setting until smooth. On the stovetop, simmer everything for 20 to 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender.

diet.low_carb: Potatoes are the point of this soup and carry most of its carbohydrate, about 240 grams across the whole pot, so a low-carb version is not possible without changing the dish. Cauliflower florets in place of the potatoes give a similar soup for a fraction of the carbohydrate, with a different flavor.
diet.gluten_free: The soup is gluten-free as written, since there is no flour. Check the labels on the broth and bacon.
diet.vegan: Use vegetable broth, replace the cream cheese and half-and-half with 1 cup of full-fat oat milk and 1/2 cup of raw cashews blended smooth, skip the bacon and cheese, and top with smoked paprika and toasted seeds or dairy-free bacon bits.

batch_1.storage_tips: Cool the soup and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days; it thickens as it sits. Freezing is not recommended, because potatoes turn grainy and the dairy can separate when thawed. If you want to freeze it, do so before adding the cream cheese and half-and-half and stir them in on reheating. Reheat on the stove over medium-low heat, stirring often, with a splash of milk or broth to loosen it, until it is steaming hot.

faqs.question: How do I thicken potato soup?
faqs.answer: Mash more of the potatoes in the pot; their starch thickens the soup without flour. You can also simmer uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes to reduce it or stir in a handful of instant mashed potato flakes.

faqs.question: Why is my potato soup gluey?
faqs.answer: Blending or overworking cooked potatoes releases too much starch and makes the soup gummy. Use a hand masher, stop when about half the potatoes are crushed, and avoid a blender or food processor.

faqs.question: Can I make potato soup ahead of time?
faqs.answer: Yes. The soup keeps 4 days in the fridge and tastes better the next day. Add fresh toppings when you serve it and thin it with broth or milk on reheating.

faqs.question: Can you freeze potato soup?
faqs.answer: You can, but the texture suffers: potatoes go grainy and dairy may separate. Freeze the soup before adding the cream cheese and half-and-half, or accept a slightly grainy result, and stir vigorously as it reheats.

batch_1.title: Breakfast Casserole
batch_1.description: An easy make-ahead breakfast casserole with sausage, sharp cheddar, eggs and bread, baked until puffed and golden and sliceable for a crowd.
secondary_keywords: breakfast casserole with sausage and cheese
intro: This breakfast casserole layers browned sausage, sharp cheddar and cubed bread in a dish, then soaks everything in a savory custard of eggs and milk. In the oven the custard sets around the bread and sausage, giving a puffed, golden top and a tender, sliceable center.

It suits a crowd because almost all the work can happen the night before. Assemble it, refrigerate it, and bake it in the morning while you make coffee. The overnight rest lets the bread absorb the custard fully, which is what keeps the casserole cohesive instead of dry on top and soggy underneath.
The flavor is savory and rich, with sage and pepper from the sausage, tang from the cheddar and a hint of mustard. Serve it with fruit or a green salad, and it feeds eight.

key_ingredients.name: Breakfast sausage
key_ingredients.role: Provides fat, salt and sage seasoning, so the casserole needs little else.

key_ingredients.name: Day-old bread cubes
key_ingredients.role: Dry bread absorbs the custard and keeps its shape instead of turning to paste.

key_ingredients.name: Eggs and whole milk
key_ingredients.role: Make the custard that sets the casserole; the ratio here gives a tender, sliceable set.

key_ingredients.name: Sharp cheddar
key_ingredients.role: Adds tang and melts into the custard and the golden top.

key_ingredients.name: Dijon mustard
key_ingredients.role: A small amount sharpens the flavor of the eggs and cheese.

ingredients: 1 tbsp unsalted butter, for the dish
8 cups (about 10 oz / 285 g) day-old white bread or sourdough, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 cups (8 oz / 225 g) shredded sharp cheddar cheese, divided
instructions: Grease a 9 by 13-inch baking dish with the butter.
Cook the sausage in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 7 to 9 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles, until browned and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.
Spread half of the bread cubes in the dish. Top with the sausage, half of the cheddar and the green onions, then add the remaining bread cubes.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, mustard, salt, pepper and garlic powder until smooth. Pour evenly over the bread and press down gently so all the cubes are moistened.
Sprinkle the remaining cheddar over the top. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 12 hours, so the bread can absorb the custard.

Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Bake uncovered for 45 to 50 minutes, until the top is golden, the casserole is puffed and set in the center, and the center reads 160°F (71°C) on an instant-read thermometer. If the top browns too quickly, cover loosely with foil.
Rest for 10 minutes so the custard finishes setting, then cut into squares and serve.
pro_tips: Use dry, day-old bread. Fresh bread turns to paste in the custard; dry cubes soak it up and keep their shape. If your bread is fresh, toast the cubes on a sheet pan at 300°F for 10 to 15 minutes first.
Let the casserole soak at least 30 minutes, and ideally overnight, so the custard reaches the center of the cubes. A short soak leaves dry pockets in the middle.
Check the center, not the edges. The casserole is done when it reads 160°F (71°C), no liquid pools when you press the middle and a knife comes out clean.
Rest the casserole for 10 minutes after baking. Egg custard continues to set as it stands, and cutting too early gives runny squares.
substitutions: Use ham, cooked bacon or breakfast links in place of the sausage; about 2 cups of chopped cooked meat.
Swap the cheddar for pepper jack, Gruyère or Swiss, or use a mix of two.
Add 2 cups of sautéed spinach, mushrooms or diced bell pepper; cook the vegetables first and squeeze out the moisture so the custard does not turn watery.

variations.air_fryer: A halved batch in a 7-inch oven-safe dish that fits your basket can be cooked in the air fryer at 320°F (160°C). Start checking at 25 minutes and cook until the center reaches 160°F (71°C), covering the top with foil if it browns too quickly.
variations.slow_cooker: Layer everything in a greased 6-quart slow cooker: bread, sausage, cheese, then the egg mixture. Cook on low for 4 to 5 hours or until the center reaches 160°F (71°C). Slow cooker casseroles come out softer and do not brown on top, so finish under the broiler for 2 minutes if you can.

diet.low_carb: Leave out the bread and use 4 cups of sautéed vegetables such as spinach, mushrooms and peppers, squeezing out the moisture, then bake in the same dish as a crustless egg bake. Carbohydrate falls to under 10 grams per serving.
diet.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free bread, dried out as described for regular bread, and check the sausage and mustard labels, since some sausages contain wheat fillers.
diet.vegan: Replace the eggs with a mixture of 1 (14 oz) block of firm tofu blended with 1 cup of plant milk, 1/4 cup of nutritional yeast and 1 tsp of turmeric, use plant-based sausage and dairy-free cheese, and bake for about 40 minutes until set. The texture is closer to a soft scramble bake than a custard.

batch_1.storage_tips: The assembled, unbaked casserole keeps in the refrigerator, covered, for up to 12 hours before baking. Refrigerate baked leftovers in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Freeze cooled, baked portions individually wrapped for up to 2 months, and thaw overnight in the fridge. Reheat squares covered with foil in a 350°F (175°C) oven for 15 to 20 minutes, or microwave a single portion for 60 to 90 seconds until it reaches 165°F (74°C).

faqs.question: Can I make breakfast casserole the night before?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better for it. Assemble the casserole, cover it and refrigerate for up to 12 hours; then bake straight from the fridge, adding 5 to 10 minutes to the baking time if needed.

faqs.question: How do I know when breakfast casserole is done?
faqs.answer: The top should be puffed and golden, the center should not jiggle, and an instant-read thermometer in the center should read 160°F (71°C). A knife inserted in the middle should come out clean.

faqs.question: Why is my breakfast casserole soggy on the bottom?
faqs.answer: Too much liquid for the amount of bread, fresh bread or a short soak are the usual causes. Use dry, day-old bread cubes, measure the milk, and let the casserole rest 10 minutes after baking.

faqs.question: Can you freeze breakfast casserole?
faqs.answer: Yes. Freeze the baked casserole in individual portions for up to 2 months, and thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.

batch_1.title: Garlic Knots
batch_1.description: Soft homemade garlic knots tossed in garlic-Parmesan butter, made from a simple yeast dough and baked in 15 minutes.
intro: Garlic knots are strips of yeast dough tied into small knots, baked until golden and tossed while hot in melted butter with garlic, Parmesan and parsley. They are a pizzeria side, traditionally made from leftover pizza dough, and this recipe makes an easy dough from scratch so you can have them without a pizza order.

The dough is a basic mix of flour, water, yeast, salt and olive oil, kneaded until smooth and left to rise once until doubled. Tying each rope into a knot gives the knots more surface to soak up the garlic butter and a chewy, tender bite in the center.

Sixteen knots take about two hours from start to finish, most of it hands-off rising time. Serve them warm with marinara for dipping, alongside pasta, soup or salad. They are at their best within an hour of baking, while the crust is still soft and the butter has not yet set.

key_ingredients.name: All-purpose flour
key_ingredients.role: Provides enough gluten for a soft, slightly chewy knot without special ingredients.

key_ingredients.name: Active dry yeast
key_ingredients.role: Makes the dough rise; it must foam in warm water to prove it is alive.

key_ingredients.name: Olive oil
key_ingredients.role: Softens the dough and adds flavor.

key_ingredients.name: Garlic butter
key_ingredients.role: Melted butter with fresh garlic, Parmesan and parsley is what makes the knots taste like a pizzeria side.

key_ingredients.name: Kosher salt
key_ingredients.role: Controls the yeast and gives the dough flavor; too little makes flat, bland bread.

ingredients: 1 cup (240 ml) warm water (105 to 110°F / 40 to 43°C)
2 1/4 tsp (1 packet / 7 g) active dry yeast
3 cups (375 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
2 tbsp olive oil, plus more for the bowl
instructions: Stir the warm water, yeast and sugar together in a large bowl and let stand for 5 minutes until foamy.

Add the flour, kosher salt and olive oil. Stir until a shaggy dough forms, then knead on a lightly floured surface for 8 minutes (or 5 to 6 minutes with a dough hook on a stand mixer) until smooth and elastic.
Transfer the dough to an oiled bowl, turn to coat, cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Line two baking sheets with parchment. Turn the dough onto a floured surface and divide it into 16 equal pieces, about 45 g (1 1/2 oz) each.
Roll each piece into a rope about 8 inches long. Tie it into a loose single knot and tuck the ends underneath. Place on the sheets 2 inches apart.
Cover and let the knots rest for 15 minutes while you heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Bake for 13 to 15 minutes, until golden brown. Rotate the pans halfway through if your oven bakes unevenly.
While the knots bake, stir the melted butter with the garlic, Parmesan and parsley.
Toss the hot knots in the garlic butter in a large bowl until coated, sprinkle with flaky salt and serve warm.
pro_tips: Check the water temperature. Water above about 115°F (46°C) can kill yeast and water that is too cool slows it, so use a thermometer or water that feels comfortably warm, not hot, on your wrist.
Knead until the dough passes the windowpane test: stretch a small piece thin and it should become translucent without tearing. Under-kneaded dough bakes into dense knots.
Tie the knots loosely. The dough expands during the second rise and in the oven, and tight knots come out dense rather than pillowy.
Stir the garlic into the melted butter while the knots bake, and toss while both are hot. Raw garlic tossed into cold butter tastes sharp; warm butter takes the edge off it.
substitutions: Use bread flour for chewier knots; the dough may need 1 to 2 extra tablespoons of water.
Instant yeast can replace active dry yeast at the same amount and does not need proofing, so you can stir it into the flour.
About 1 lb of store-bought pizza dough replaces the homemade dough; divide, roll and tie as in the recipe, and skip the first rise.

variations.air_fryer: Working in batches, air fry the shaped, risen knots at 350°F (175°C) for 8 to 10 minutes until golden, spacing them so they do not touch, and toss in the garlic butter while hot. Expect a slightly paler top than from the oven.
variations.slow_cooker: A slow cooker is not suited to garlic knots, which need dry oven heat to brown and crisp; it would steam the dough into pale, gummy rolls. Use the slow cooker for the marinara you serve with them instead.

diet.low_carb: Bread dough is high in carbohydrate, about 18 grams per knot, so a real low-carb version needs a different dough. A fathead-style dough made from mozzarella and almond flour can be tied and baked the same way, but it is a different recipe.
diet.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free bread flour blend that contains xanthan gum, and expect a wetter, stickier dough that you shape with oiled hands; the knots will be softer and will not stay chewy.
diet.vegan: Replace the butter with vegan butter or olive oil and use nutritional yeast in place of the Parmesan. The dough itself contains no dairy or eggs.

batch_1.storage_tips: Garlic knots are best the day they are made. Store leftovers in an airtight container or bag at room temperature for up to 2 days. Do not refrigerate them: the fridge makes bread go stale faster than the counter does. Freeze baked knots, before tossing in the garlic butter if you can, in a freezer bag for up to 2 months. Reheat at 350°F (175°C) for 6 to 8 minutes from room temperature, or 10 to 12 minutes from frozen, then toss in freshly melted garlic butter. Microwaving makes them chewy.

faqs.question: Why are my garlic knots dense?
faqs.answer: Common causes are under-kneading, dead yeast or a rise that was too short. Make sure the yeast foams in the first step, knead until the dough is smooth and elastic, and let it double in size before shaping.

faqs.question: Can I make garlic knots ahead of time?
faqs.answer: Yes. Bake them and toss in the butter just before serving, or shape the knots and refrigerate them on the sheet, covered, for up to 12 hours, then let them stand 30 minutes before baking.

faqs.question: Can I use store-bought pizza dough for garlic knots?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use about 1 pound of pizza dough, let it come to room temperature, then divide, tie and bake as in the recipe. Skip the first rise; a 15-minute rest after shaping is enough.

faqs.question: Can you freeze garlic knots?
faqs.answer: Yes. Freeze baked, cooled knots in a freezer bag for up to 2 months and reheat in a 350°F oven until hot, then toss in fresh garlic butter.

batch_1.title: Protein Muffins
batch_1.description: Soft blueberry protein muffins blended from oats, cottage cheese, eggs and vanilla protein powder, with about 9 grams of protein each.
intro: These protein muffins are made by blending rolled oats, cottage cheese, eggs, milk, honey and vanilla protein powder into a smooth batter, folding in blueberries and baking for about 24 minutes. Each muffin has about 9 grams of protein and 145 calories, so two make a filling high protein breakfast.

Cottage cheese and eggs carry most of the protein and keep the crumb moist, which matters because whey protein powder can make baked goods dry and rubbery if it is the main structure. Blending the oats turns them into a fine flour, so the muffins bake tender without any wheat flour.
The muffins are lightly sweet, with a soft, cake-like crumb and bursts of blueberry. They keep for days in the fridge, freeze well, and reheat in seconds for busy mornings.

key_ingredients.name: Rolled oats
key_ingredients.role: Blended into flour, they replace wheat flour and add fiber.

key_ingredients.name: Cottage cheese
key_ingredients.role: Adds protein and moisture; blend it fully so there are no curds.

key_ingredients.name: Eggs
key_ingredients.role: Set the structure and add protein.

key_ingredients.name: Vanilla whey protein powder
key_ingredients.role: Contributes about 24 grams of protein per scoop; use 1 scoop for 12 muffins.

key_ingredients.name: Honey
key_ingredients.role: Sweetens and holds moisture, which helps offset the drying effect of protein powder.

ingredients: 1/2 cup (120 ml) milk of your choice
1/3 cup (113 g) honey or maple syrup
1 scoop (about 30 g) vanilla whey protein powder
3/4 cup (110 g) fresh or frozen blueberries
Cooking spray or paper liners, for the pan
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners or grease it well with cooking spray.
Add the oats, cottage cheese, eggs, milk, honey, protein powder, baking powder, vanilla, cinnamon and salt to a blender. Blend for 30 to 45 seconds until smooth, scraping down the sides once.
Let the batter stand for 5 minutes so the oats hydrate and thicken it.
Fold in the blueberries by hand. If using frozen berries, do not thaw them first.
Divide the batter among the 12 cups, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes, until the tops spring back when pressed and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
pro_tips: Blend the batter until completely smooth. Any cottage cheese curds left behind bake into wet spots, and coarse oats make a gritty crumb.
Do not overbake. Whey protein turns muffins dry and rubbery quickly, so start checking at 22 minutes and pull them as soon as a toothpick comes out clean.
Use a whey or whey-casein blend labeled vanilla. Plant protein powders absorb far more liquid; if you use pea or soy protein, add 2 to 3 tablespoons more milk.
Scrape the honey fully into the blender. The sweetness and the moisture both depend on it, and a lightly oiled spoon makes it slide out cleanly.
substitutions: Use plain Greek yogurt in place of cottage cheese for a smoother batter; the protein is similar.
Replace the blueberries with chopped banana, raspberries or dark chocolate chips (about 1/3 cup); chocolate chips add sugar and fat.
Unsweetened applesauce, 1/4 cup, can replace half of the honey for a less sweet muffin; the texture will be slightly denser.

variations.air_fryer: Silicone muffin cups fit most air fryer baskets. Fill 6 cups about three-quarters full and air fry at 320°F (160°C), start checking at 14 minutes and cook until a toothpick comes out clean; bake the second half in a second batch. Air fryer muffins rise a little less and brown faster on top.
variations.slow_cooker: A slow cooker is not a good fit for muffins, which need dry heat to set and brown. For a slow cooker breakfast with the same ingredients, pour the batter into a greased 4-quart cooker without liners and cook on low for 2 to 3 hours until set, for a soft baked-oatmeal cake, then slice and serve.

diet.low_carb: Rolled oats and honey make these muffins about 21 grams of carbohydrate each, so they are not low-carb. A different recipe using almond flour and a sugar-free sweetener would be a better choice.
diet.gluten_free: Use certified gluten-free rolled oats, since regular oats are often processed alongside wheat, and check the protein powder label.
diet.vegan: The muffins rely on eggs and cottage cheese for structure and protein, so a vegan version needs a rebuilt recipe: blended oats with soft tofu, plant milk, ground flax eggs, maple syrup and a plant protein powder, baked at 375°F for 22 to 25 minutes. The result is denser.

batch_1.storage_tips: Cool the muffins completely. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days, because the cottage cheese and eggs make them perishable; they keep at room temperature for about 1 day. Freeze in a freezer bag for up to 3 months and thaw overnight in the fridge. To reheat, microwave one muffin for 20 to 30 seconds, or warm in a 350°F (175°C) oven for 8 to 10 minutes until heated through.

faqs.question: How much protein is in each muffin?
faqs.answer: About 9 grams per muffin using a vanilla whey protein powder with roughly 24 grams of protein per 30 gram scoop. The figure varies with the brand of protein powder and cottage cheese, so check your labels.

faqs.question: Why are my protein muffins dry?
faqs.answer: Whey protein bakes dry if the muffins go too long in the oven or if the powder is a large part of the batter. Bake just until a toothpick comes out clean, and keep to a single scoop for 12 muffins.

faqs.question: Can I make protein muffins without protein powder?
faqs.answer: Yes. Leave out the scoop and replace it with 1/4 cup of rolled oats blended into the batter. The muffins will have about 6 to 7 grams of protein each rather than 9.

faqs.question: Can you freeze protein muffins?
faqs.answer: Yes. Freeze cooled muffins in a freezer bag for up to 3 months, and thaw them overnight in the refrigerator or microwave from frozen for 45 to 60 seconds.

batch_1.title: Slow Cooker Beef Chili
batch_1.description: Thick, hearty beef chili with kidney and black beans, simmered all day in the slow cooker with chili powder, cumin and smoked paprika.
intro: This slow cooker beef chili is thick, meaty and lightly spicy, built from ground beef browned with onion and bell pepper, then simmered for 8 hours with crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, kidney and black beans, chili powder, cumin and smoked paprika. It is an easy recipe for any 6-quart slow cooker, including a Crockpot.

Browning the beef and onion in a skillet before they go in the pot is the step that separates good chili from watery chili: it builds a roasted, savory base that a slow cooker cannot create by itself. The long, low cook then does what it does best, blending the spices into the tomato and softening the beans until the chili is thick enough to hold a spoon upright.

It feeds eight, freezes well and improves on the second day. Top it with cheddar, sour cream, green onions or crushed tortilla chips. The recipe is forgiving: an extra half hour on low does no harm, which makes it easy to fit around a working day.

key_ingredients.name: Ground beef, 85% lean
key_ingredients.role: Enough fat for flavor and richness; drain the excess after browning.

key_ingredients.name: Chili powder, cumin and smoked paprika
key_ingredients.role: The backbone of the flavor; cooking them with the meat first deepens their taste.

key_ingredients.name: Crushed tomatoes and tomato sauce
key_ingredients.role: Make up the body of the chili; crushed tomatoes give texture and sauce gives smoothness.

key_ingredients.name: Kidney and black beans
key_ingredients.role: Add fiber, protein and thickness; canned saves hours.

key_ingredients.name: Brown sugar
key_ingredients.role: A little sweetness balances the acid in the tomatoes.

ingredients: 1 (15 oz / 425 g) can kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 (15 oz / 425 g) can black beans, drained and rinsed
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 cup (4 oz / 113 g) shredded cheddar cheese, for serving
instructions: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it into crumbles. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook 4 minutes more until softened.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Drain off the excess fat and transfer the meat mixture to a 6-quart slow cooker.
Add the crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, beans, beef broth, brown sugar, salt and pepper. Stir well.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, or on high for 4 to 5 hours, until the chili is thick and the flavors have blended.
Taste and adjust the salt, adding a splash of vinegar or a squeeze of lime if it tastes flat.
Ladle into bowls and top with the cheddar and any other toppings.
pro_tips: Brown the beef until it has color, not until it turns gray. The browned bits in the skillet and on the meat are the source of the chili's deep, roasted flavor.
Drain excess fat before it goes in the slow cooker. A slow cooker traps liquid, so leftover fat floats on top and makes the chili greasy instead of rich.
Cook the spices with the meat for a minute. Toasting chili powder and cumin in a little fat blooms their flavor, which dry spices added straight to the pot never fully reach.
If the chili is too thin at the end, cook it uncovered on high for 30 minutes, or mash a half cup of the beans against the side of the pot and stir them in.
substitutions: Ground turkey or ground chuck can replace the beef; turkey is leaner, so add a tablespoon of oil when browning.
Pinto or cannellini beans work in place of kidney or black beans, and you can add a third can if you like a beanier chili.
Add a diced jalapeño or 1/2 teaspoon of cayenne for heat, or a tablespoon of unsweetened cocoa for a darker, deeper flavor.

variations.air_fryer: The air fryer is not suited to a chili, but it is good for toppings. Air fry corn tortilla strips, tossed with oil and salt, at 375°F (190°C) for 4 to 6 minutes for a crunchy topping.
variations.slow_cooker: This recipe is the slow cooker method. In an Instant Pot, brown the beef on the sauté setting, add the remaining ingredients, and pressure cook on high for 25 minutes with a 15-minute natural release. On the stovetop, simmer covered on low for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, stirring occasionally.

diet.low_carb: Beans and tomatoes account for most of the carbohydrate, about 26 grams per serving. Leaving out the beans and brown sugar and adding a second can of diced tomatoes brings it down to roughly 16 grams per serving.
diet.gluten_free: The chili is gluten-free as written. Check the labels on the broth, tomato sauce and chili powder, since some brands add wheat-based thickeners.
diet.vegan: Replace the beef with 1 cup of dry brown lentils and 1 diced portobello mushroom, add 1 extra cup of broth for the lentils, use vegetable broth and skip the cheese. Lentils cook through in the same 8 hours.

batch_1.storage_tips: Cool the chili and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 5 days; it tastes better on the second day. Freeze in portions for up to 3 months and thaw overnight in the fridge. Reheat on the stove over medium heat, stirring often, until steaming hot, or microwave in 60-second bursts, stirring in between, adding a splash of water or broth if it has thickened.

faqs.question: How do I thicken slow cooker chili?
faqs.answer: Remove the lid and cook on high for 30 minutes, or mash about 1/2 cup of the beans and stir them in. A tablespoon of cornmeal or masa harina stirred in during the last 20 minutes also thickens the chili and adds a corn flavor.

faqs.question: Do I have to brown the meat before slow cooking chili?
faqs.answer: You can skip it for convenience, but the chili will taste flatter and greasier. Browning takes about 10 minutes and adds a roasted flavor. It also lets you drain the fat, which a slow cooker would otherwise leave floating on top.

faqs.question: Can I cook chili on high instead of low?
faqs.answer: Yes. High takes 4 to 5 hours instead of 8. The result is similar, though low heat blends the flavors more gently and is less likely to catch on the edges.

faqs.question: Can you freeze chili?
faqs.answer: Yes, chili is one of the best freezer meals. Cool it fully, freeze it in portions for up to 3 months and thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating on the stove.
